_header.purpose: The frozen task set model_resolver.py's --qualify runs against a candidate tag. Every task mirrors a REAL, already-tested contract from this repository (see each task's source_reference), so a candidate is graded on work this repository actually needed, not a synthetic benchmark.
_header.coder_vs_writer_evidence: A coder task is graded by run_qualification_tasks executing a real assertion against the candidate's generated code (see model_resolver.py, _build_coder_verify_command): the candidate either reproduces the mirrored function's observable behaviour on every case, or it does not. A writer task has no such oracle for whether the prose is GOOD - it can only be gated on deterministic, mechanical properties (structure, language, length, frontmatter keys; hygiene is enforced upstream by ollama_bridge.run_bridge before either gate ever runs). Passing every writer task in this set proves the candidate follows format instructions; it does not prove its prose is good. A --qualify win driven mostly by writer-task passes is weaker evidence than one driven by coder-task passes, and should be read that way.
_header.structure_gate_parameterisation: Measured earlier in this plan: a FIXED five-heading structure gate wrongly failed a good generation whose brief had deliberately asked for two sections only. Every writer task below therefore carries its OWN required_sections list (two for writer-vault-two-section, four for writer-atomic-resource-note, one for writer-changelog-entry); model_resolver.py's writer check reads that list per task and never falls back to a constant heading list. This file's shape is itself the fix: the requirement lives with the task, not with the checker.
_header.changing_this_file: Adding, removing, or editing a task changes what 'beating the incumbent' means. A change here should be a deliberate, reviewed edit, not an incidental one; it does not retroactively change local-model-state.json's history, which records the task set's outcome at the time each qualification ran.
